newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anzoil says Vietnam fracturing ops to begin.
newsitem.headline: Anzoil says Vietnam fracturing ops to begin.

text.p: Operations to determine if a natural gas find in the onshore Hanoi Basin of Vietnam is commercial are expected to begin next week, Anzoil NL said on Wednesday.
Fracturing equipment is being set up at the D14-3 well and fracture operations are expected to commence on 15 May, it said.

The fracturing operations would determine if commercial flow rates can be achieved which would enable gas contract negotiations to be concluded to supply the Tien Hai power station, the company has said.
The D14-3 well was shut in on April 30 after flowing gas at a stabilised rate of 180,000 cubic feet per day, Anzoil said.
D14-3, the second appraisal well on the Song Tra Ly D14 gas field, was drilled to a final total depth of 4,903 metres.
D14-3 encountered gas in 38 metres of net sand in Zones One, Two and Three as compared to 49 metres in the D14-1x discovery well and 43 metres in the D14-2 appraisal well.
Anzoil's majority-owned Anzoil (Asia) Pte Ltd is the operator of the Production Sharing Contract for the onshore Hanoi Basin.
Anzoil is in dispute with Frontier Petroleum NL, the other partner in Anzoil (Asia), over their respective stakes which were Anzoil 80 percent and Frontier 20 percent.
The dispute began in February when Frontier failed to meet a drawdown notice of US$852,435 issued by Anzoil (Asia) to fund exploration and appraisal.

On Tuesday, Anzoil won the first round of a legal battle over the Anzoil (Asia) shareholders' agreement when the Western Australian Supreme Court affirmed Anzoil's interpretation of one factor in the agreement's dilution formula for default.
The decision meant the increase in Anzoil's equity in Anzoil (Asia) is likely to be at least 4.4672 percent, Anzoil said.
The case goes back to court on May 16 to determine what the total dilution will be as a result of Frontier's default on the February drawdown notice, Anzoil said.
